drills.title: Long passes into a target box
drills.summary: Lofted passes into a box 20 m away, where the receiver must control the ball inside the box.
drills.setup: Two 10 x 10 m boxes with a 20 m zone between them. One player in each box with a ball between them; several pairs can work side by side.
instructions: A1 plays a lofted pass into the far box.
A2 must control the ball and keep it inside the box.
A2 takes a touch out of their feet and plays a lofted pass back.
A point for every pass controlled inside the box; swap feet every five passes.
coaching_points: Take a touch out of your feet so you can approach at a slight angle.
Plant your standing foot beside the ball and lean back a little.
Strike the bottom half of the ball with the laces or instep and follow through towards the target.
Receiver: judge the flight early, move under it and cushion it with foot, thigh or chest.

variations.title: Along the ground, 15 m
variations.change: Boxes 15 m apart; drive the pass along the ground before trying to lift it.
variations.setup: Two 10 x 10 m boxes with a 15 m zone between them. One player in each box with a ball between them.
coaching_points: Strike through the middle of the ball with the laces to keep it low and firm.
Point your standing foot at the target.
Receiver: move into line with the ball and cushion it inside the box.

variations.title: Lofted passes over 20 m
variations.change: Lofted passes into a box 20 m away; control inside the box.

variations.title: Over a defender in the middle
variations.change: A defender in the middle zone tries to block or intercept, so the pass must go over them.
variations.setup: Two 10 x 10 m boxes with a 20 m zone between them. One player in each box and a defender in the middle zone, who must stay in it.
instructions: The defender in the middle zone tries to block or intercept every pass.
Pass over them into the far box; the receiver controls it inside the box.
An intercepted pass: the defender swaps with the passer.

variations.title: 4v2, then switch first time
variations.change: Keep the ball 4v2 in one box; after four passes, switch first time into the far box.
variations.setup: Two 14 x 12 m boxes with a 20 m zone between them. Four attackers and two defenders in one box, one target player in the other.
instructions: Four attackers keep the ball from two defenders in the first box.
After four passes, any attacker may switch it first time to the target player.
The target controls it in the box and lofts it back to restart.
A point for every switch controlled in the box; defenders swap in when they win it.
coaching_points: Have the switch in mind before the ball arrives: open your body to the far box.
First time means the ball must be moving across you, not at you: get side-on.
Strike under the ball and through it to get height and distance.
Supporting players keep wide angles so the pass that sets up the switch is on.

media.caption: Lofted pass into the far box; the receiver controls it inside the box

steps.label: A1 takes a touch out of their feet, at a slight angle to the target
Lofted pass into the far box; A2 moves to get under the flight early
A2 controls it inside the box with the first touch
Touch out of the feet, then a lofted pass back

media.caption: Harder: the pass must go over a defender in the middle zone

steps.label: A1 takes a touch out of their feet; the defender moves across to block the line
Lofted pass over the defender; A2 moves under the flight
A2 controls inside the box; the defender turns to face them
A2 lofts it back over the defender

media.caption: Hardest: keep it 4v2 in one box, then switch first time to the other

steps.label: A1 passes to A2; A3 and A4 open up to give angles
Pass two: A2 to A4 as the defenders shift
Pass three: A4 to A3 across the box
Pass four: A3 sets it back to A1
After four passes, A1 switches first time into the far box
T controls inside the box and lofts it back to restart

drills.title: Crosses from a wide channel to near and far post runs
drills.summary: A winger dribbles into the end zone and crosses for two runners attacking the near and far post.
drills.setup: A goal with a goalkeeper. A 6 m wide channel on one side, with an end zone marked by a cone line 8 m from the byline. One winger with the balls at the top of the channel, two runners in the middle about 20 m out.
instructions: The winger dribbles down the channel into the end zone.
As the winger arrives in the end zone, the runners split: one to the near post, one to the far post.
The winger crosses low and driven, or cuts it back; the runners finish first time if they can.
Rotate winger, runners and the next pair; switch the channel to the other side halfway through.
Outfield players play with their feet only in this drill: no headers. Heading has its own drill, for U12 and older, following the FA's heading guidance.
coaching_points: Winger: look up before crossing to see where the runners and the goalkeeper are.
Strike across the ball with the laces or instep; aim for space in front of the runner, not at them.
Runners: hold your run, then arrive as the ball does; don't wait on the spot.
Near-post runner attacks the front of the goal; far-post runner arrives behind them.

variations.title: Cut back a still ball
variations.change: The winger starts in the end zone with the ball still and cuts it back along the ground to one runner.
variations.setup: A goal with a goalkeeper and a 6 m wide channel with an end zone 8 m from the byline. The winger stands in the end zone with the ball; one runner waits about 18 m out.
instructions: The runner jogs towards the penalty spot.
The winger cuts the ball back along the ground into the runner's path.
The runner finishes first time; swap roles after three goes each.
Outfield players play with their feet only in this drill: no headers. Heading has its own drill, for U12 and older, following the FA's heading guidance.
coaching_points: Winger: pass across the ball into space in front of the runner.
Runner: time the run so you meet the ball, don't stop and wait for it.
Finish with the inside of the foot for accuracy.

variations.title: Dribble in and cross to two runners
variations.change: The winger dribbles into the end zone and crosses for near and far post runs.

variations.title: Early cross or byline
variations.change: A passive defender in the channel: if they block the way to the byline, cross early and deep; if not, go to the byline.
variations.setup: As the base, plus a passive defender in the channel who chooses to stand deep or step up to the winger.
instructions: The defender in the channel stands deep or steps up; they don't tackle.
If the way to the byline is blocked, cross early and deep, behind the goalkeeper towards the far post.
If it's open, dribble into the end zone and cross or cut back.
The runners read the winger's choice and adjust their runs.
Outfield players play with their feet only in this drill: no headers. Heading has its own drill, for U12 and older, following the FA's heading guidance.
coaching_points: Decide early: look at the defender's position before you reach them.
An early cross goes into the space between the goalkeeper and the defenders.
Runners: watch the winger's body shape to read which cross is coming.

variations.title: Live winger and 2v2 in the box
variations.change: A live defender on the winger and two defenders marking the runners in the box.
variations.setup: As the base, plus a live defender in the channel and two defenders marking the runners in the box.
instructions: The winger has to beat or get past the channel defender before crossing.
The runners move to lose their markers; the winger picks the cross that's on.
Defenders who win the ball score by passing it to the coach.
Outfield players play with their feet only in this drill: no headers. Heading has its own drill, for U12 and older, following the FA's heading guidance.
coaching_points: Winger: create a yard of space with a touch past the defender, then cross before they recover.
Runners: one run can drag a defender away to make space for the other.
Vary the cross: near post, far post, or cut-back, depending on where the space is.

media.caption: Easier: cut back a still ball from the end zone to a runner

steps.label: The winger stands in the end zone with the ball; F1 runs towards the penalty spot
Cut-back along the ground into F1's path
F1 finishes first time

media.caption: Dribble into the end zone and cross to near and far post runs

steps.label: The winger dribbles down the channel; the runners hold their runs
Into the end zone: the runners split, one to the near post and one to the far post
Low, driven cross into the near-post runner's path
F1 finishes at the near post

media.caption: Harder: the defender blocks the way to the byline, so cross early to the far post

steps.label: The winger dribbles at the defender; the runners start their runs
The defender stands deep to block the way to the byline
Early, deep cross from in front of the defender, behind the goalkeeper towards the far post
F2 finishes at the far post

media.caption: Hardest: a live defender on the winger and 2v2 in the box

steps.label: The winger beats the defender on the outside and drives into the end zone
F1 drags their marker to the near post; F2 checks back towards the penalty spot
Cut-back to F2, in the space the near-post run left
F2 finishes before the defenders recover

media.caption: Source: England Football – Attacking session: width for deception

drills.title: Heading from a partner's throw
drills.summary: Head an underarm throw back to a partner with good technique, using a lighter ball and the FA's limits on headers.
drills.setup: Pairs 5 m apart, one ball per pair. Use a lighter ball: size 3 for U12–U13 and size 4 for U14–U16, at the lowest pressure the Laws of the Game allow.
instructions: The thrower throws underarm to the header's forehead height.
The header steps in and heads it back into the thrower's hands.
Swap roles after each player's headers.
Count each player's headers. FA guidance: one heading session a week, at most 5 headers each for U12–U13 and 10 for U14–U16; keep heading practice for U17–U18 as low as possible.
coaching_points: Eyes open and mouth closed.
Head the ball with the forehead, at the hairline.
Keep the neck firm and move the body through the ball: the power comes from the body, not a nod of the head.
Quality over quantity: a few good headers, then stop.

variations.title: Kneeling, from 3 m
variations.change: The header kneels and the thrower throws gently from 3 m, so the header learns the contact without moving.
variations.setup: Pairs 3 m apart, the header kneeling. A lighter ball: size 3 for U12–U13 and size 4 for U14–U16, at the lowest pressure the Laws of the Game allow.
instructions: The header kneels; the thrower throws gently underarm from 3 m.
Head it back into the thrower's hands using the forehead.
Swap roles after each player's headers.
Count each player's headers. FA guidance: one heading session a week, at most 5 headers each for U12–U13 and 10 for U14–U16; keep heading practice for U17–U18 as low as possible.
coaching_points: Eyes open and mouth closed.
Lean back a little, then bring the upper body forward to meet the ball.
Contact with the forehead, not the top of the head.

variations.title: Standing, from 5 m
variations.change: Standing, 5 m apart: step in and head it back into the thrower's hands.

variations.title: Head down into a small goal
variations.change: A throw from the side; head it down towards a small goal 4 m away.
variations.setup: A small goal; the header stands 4 m from it, the thrower 3 m to one side. A lighter ball: size 3 for U12–U13 and size 4 for U14–U16, at low pressure.
instructions: The thrower throws underarm from the side at forehead height.
The header turns the head and neck towards the goal and heads the ball down at it.
Swap roles after each player's headers.
Count each player's headers. FA guidance: one heading session a week, at most 5 headers each for U12–U13 and 10 for U14–U16; keep heading practice for U17–U18 as low as possible.
coaching_points: Get across the line of the ball so you can head it towards the goal.
Head the top half of the ball to send it down.
Eyes open: watch the ball onto your forehead.

variations.title: Attack a high throw and clear it
variations.change: A higher throw from 8 m: two steps in, jump and head it high and far towards a gate behind the thrower.
variations.setup: Pairs 8 m apart and a cone gate 4 m behind the thrower. A lighter ball: size 3 for U12–U13 and size 4 for U14–U16, at low pressure.
instructions: The thrower throws higher, underarm, from 8 m.
The header takes two steps, jumps off one foot and heads it high and far towards the gate.
Swap roles after each player's headers.
Count each player's headers. FA guidance: one heading session a week, at most 5 headers each for U12–U13 and 10 for U14–U16; keep heading practice for U17–U18 as low as possible.
coaching_points: Attack the ball: meet it at the highest point you can reach, don't let it land on you.
Take off from one foot and use your arms for balance, not to lead with the elbows.
Head through the bottom half of the ball for height and distance.

media.caption: Head an underarm throw back into the partner's hands

steps.label: Underarm throw to forehead height; the header steps in to meet it
Head it back with the forehead, eyes open, into the thrower's hands
Step back to the start; the next throw

media.caption: Harder: head down into a small goal from a throw from the side

steps.label: Underarm throw from the side, at forehead height
Turn the head and neck towards the goal and head down, aiming to bounce it just in front of the goal
Collect the ball; after their headers, swap roles

media.caption: Hardest: attack a high throw and head it high and far

steps.label: A higher throw from 8 m; two steps in and jump
Head through the bottom half of the ball: high and far, back over the thrower towards the gate
The thrower collects it; after their headers, swap roles

media.caption: Source: The FA – updated heading guidance for youth training

drills.title: Throw-ins to keep the ball
drills.summary: Receivers move to get free from a throw-in; the thrower picks the free player and the team keeps the ball.
drills.setup: A 20 m stretch of touchline and 15 m in from it. Two cone gates on the end line the team attacks towards: one near the touchline, one infield. A thrower on the line, two receivers and one defender on the pitch. If your league uses kick-ins instead, play the ball in along the ground from the line.
instructions: The two receivers move to get free; the defender marks one of them.
The thrower throws to the free player, then steps onto the pitch as an option.
The team attacks along the line and scores by dribbling through either gate; the defender scores by winning the ball and dribbling over the opposite end line.
A foul throw goes to the defender. Rotate after three throws each.
coaching_points: Thrower: both feet on the ground on or behind the line; ball from behind the head with both hands.
Look before you throw: pick the free player, not the nearest one.
Receivers: one goes down the line, one comes short; check away first, then time your move with the thrower.
Throw to feet or thigh so it's easy to control, and step straight on to be an option.

variations.title: No defender: a legal throw to a moving partner
variations.change: No defender: practise a legal throw to a partner who checks away and comes short.
variations.setup: Pairs along a touchline: a thrower on the line and a receiver 6 m away.
instructions: The receiver checks away from the thrower, then comes short into space.
The thrower throws to their feet, using a legal throw.
The receiver controls and passes back to the thrower, who has stepped onto the pitch.
Swap after five throws.
coaching_points: Both feet on the ground, on or behind the line.
Both hands on the ball, from behind the head, in one movement.
Throw to the receiver's feet, as they arrive in the space.

variations.title: Two receivers against a defender
variations.change: Two receivers against one defender: pick the free player.

variations.title: 3v2
variations.change: Three receivers against two defenders: the thrower has to pick the free one.
variations.setup: A 20 m stretch of touchline and 15 m in from it. Two cone gates on the end line the team attacks towards: one near the touchline, one infield. A thrower on the line, three receivers and two defenders on the pitch.
instructions: Three receivers move to get free; two defenders mark.
The thrower throws to the free player and steps on as an option.
Score by dribbling through either gate; defenders score by winning the ball and dribbling over the opposite end line.
Rotate after three throws each.

variations.title: Quick throw within five seconds
variations.change: The coach hands the thrower a new ball straight away; throw within five seconds, before the defenders reset.
variations.setup: As the base, with a coach on the touchline holding spare balls. Defenders start out of position, as if play has just stopped.
instructions: The coach hands the thrower a new ball as soon as the last one goes out.
Throw within five seconds to a free player, before the defenders are set.
Score by dribbling through either gate; a throw after five seconds goes to the defenders.
If nobody is free, a throw to a marked player is fine: keeping the ball matters more than speed.
coaching_points: Get to the ball fast, but look before you throw.
Receivers: move straight away; the quick throw only works if someone is free.
A quick throw down the line can catch defenders still walking back.

media.caption: Easier: a legal throw to a partner who checks away, then comes short

steps.label: A1 checks away, down the line
Then comes short into space; the thrower throws to their feet
A1 controls and passes back to the thrower, who has stepped onto the pitch

media.caption: The receivers move to get free; the thrower picks the free one

steps.label: Both receivers check away; the defender follows A1 down the line
A2 comes short; a throw to their feet, and the defender leaves A1 to close A2
A1 is free: A2 plays it down the line; the thrower steps on as another option
A1 dribbles through the gate near the touchline

media.caption: Harder: 3v2, so the thrower has to pick the free player

steps.label: All three receivers move; the two defenders mark A1 and A2
A3 drops off, unmarked; a throw to their feet
The thrower steps on; A3 plays it back to them as D2 comes across
The thrower plays it down the line to A1, who has spun away from D1
A1 dribbles through the gate near the touchline

media.caption: Hardest: a quick throw before the defenders are set

steps.label: The ball has gone out; the coach hands the thrower a new ball straight away
Within five seconds: a throw down the line to A2, before the defenders get back
A2 drives along the line as D2 chases
A2 dribbles through the gate near the touchline

drills.title: Play out from the back against a press
drills.summary: A goalkeeper and three players play out through gates against pressers, choosing the safe option when they're pressed.
drills.setup: A 30 x 25 m area from the goal line, with three 3 m gates along the far line: left, centre and right. A goalkeeper and three players (two wide, one central) against two pressers, who start near the gates.
instructions: Every attack starts with the goalkeeper; the pressers go as the goalkeeper plays the first pass.
The goalkeeper's team scores by dribbling through any gate.
If the pressers win the ball, they attack the goal.
Playing the ball out of play on purpose when nothing is on doesn't lose a point: the coach restarts with the goalkeeper.
Swap the pressers every five attacks.
coaching_points: Look before you receive, so you know where the pressure is coming from.
Open your body so you can see both sides of the pitch.
If you're pressed and nothing is on, choose the safe option: back to the goalkeeper, wide, or out of play.
Talk to the receiver: 'time', 'man on', 'back'.
Move the ball quickly: two pressers can't cover a fast switch.

variations.title: One presser
variations.change: Only one presser, so there's more time to look and choose.
variations.setup: A 30 x 25 m area from the goal line, with three gates along the far line. A goalkeeper and three players against one presser.
coaching_points: Look before you receive: where is the presser?
Play away from the presser, to the player they can't reach.
If they're close, a pass back to the goalkeeper is always fine.

variations.title: Two pressers
variations.change: Two pressers against the goalkeeper and three players.

variations.title: Three pressers, eight seconds
variations.change: Three pressers, and the goalkeeper's team has eight seconds to get through a gate.
variations.setup: A 30 x 25 m area from the goal line, with three gates along the far line. A goalkeeper and three players against three pressers.
instructions: Every attack starts with the goalkeeper; three pressers go as the first pass is played.
Score by dribbling through any gate within eight seconds.
If the pressers win the ball, they attack the goal.
Playing it out of play on purpose when nothing is on doesn't lose a point: the coach restarts with the goalkeeper.

variations.title: Two touches, and a pressers' goal counts double
variations.change: As before, but at most two touches each, and a pressers' goal counts double.
variations.setup: A 30 x 25 m area from the goal line, with three gates along the far line. A goalkeeper and three players against three pressers.
instructions: Three pressers; the goalkeeper's team has eight seconds and at most two touches each.
Score by dribbling through any gate; a pressers' goal counts double.
Playing it out of play on purpose when nothing is on doesn't lose a point.
coaching_points: Know your next pass before the ball arrives.
Stay calm: a safe pass back is better than a risky one through the middle.
Keep talking: the receiver needs to know where the press is coming from.

media.caption: Easier: one presser, so there is time to look and choose

steps.label: The goalkeeper passes to A1; the others open up
A1 sees the presser coming and passes into A3 before they arrive
A3 turns away from the presser and dribbles through the middle gate

media.caption: Two pressers: play back to the goalkeeper, then out the other side

steps.label: The goalkeeper passes to A1; the others open up as the pressers start
A1 is pressed and A3 is covered: the safe option, back to the goalkeeper
The goalkeeper switches it to A2, away from the press
A2 plays inside to A3 before P2 arrives
A3 turns and dribbles through the right-hand gate

media.caption: Harder: three pressers; get out within eight seconds

steps.label: The goalkeeper passes to A2; three pressers come forward
A2 is pressed with A3 marked: a pass back to the goalkeeper
First time to A1, who has dropped wide
Nothing on and P1 closing: A1 plays it safely out of play, and the coach restarts with the goalkeeper

drills.title: Receive and turn to the colour the coach shows
drills.summary: Receive a pass, check the coach's colour card over the shoulder and turn through the matching gate, over long blocks.
drills.setup: A 20 x 20 m square with a 3 m gate in the middle of each side, each a different colour: red, blue, yellow and green. A passer stands by the green gate, a receiver in the middle, and the coach behind the receiver holding a bib of each colour.
instructions: The passer plays the ball in.
As the ball travels, the receiver checks over their shoulder: the coach holds up a coloured bib.
The receiver turns and dribbles through that gate, then dribbles back and passes to the passer.
Keep a count of correct turns in a row. Blocks of three minutes; swap roles after each block.
coaching_points: Look over your shoulder while the ball is travelling, not once it's arrived.
Receive across your body with the foot furthest from the ball, so you can turn either way.
Concentrate for the whole block: the coach changes colour at different times.
Made a mistake? Forget it and get ready for the next ball.

variations.title: Coach calls the colour
variations.change: The coach calls the colour out loud as the ball travels, so the receiver doesn't need to look.
instructions: The passer plays the ball in.
As the ball travels, the coach calls out a colour.
The receiver turns and dribbles through that gate, then dribbles back and passes to the passer.
Blocks of two minutes; swap roles after each block.
coaching_points: Listen for the call while the ball is coming.
Receive across your body so you can turn either way.
Keep going for the whole block, even after a mistake.

variations.title: Coach shows a colour card
variations.change: The coach holds up a coloured bib behind the receiver, who must look over their shoulder to see it.

variations.title: Turn the opposite way
variations.change: Turn through the gate opposite the colour shown: red means the blue gate, yellow means the green gate.
instructions: The passer plays the ball in; the coach holds up a coloured bib.
The receiver turns and dribbles through the gate opposite that colour.
Dribble back and pass to the passer.
Keep a count of correct turns in a row. Blocks of three minutes; swap roles after each block.
coaching_points: See the colour, then think of the opposite before the ball arrives.
Don't rush: a correct turn beats a quick wrong one.
Lost count after a mistake? Start again at zero, straight away.

variations.title: Two cues, a defender, and 'next'
variations.change: The card shows a colour and a number of touches, a passive defender tries to block the turn, and after a mistake the receiver says 'next' and plays again within three seconds.
variations.setup: As the base, plus a passive defender in the square. The coach holds a coloured bib in one hand and shows a number of fingers with the other.
instructions: The passer plays the ball in; the coach shows a colour and a number of touches (one, two or three).
The receiver turns through that gate, using exactly that many touches before passing back; if the defender blocks that side, they turn the other way.
After a mistake, the receiver says 'next' and the next ball comes within three seconds.
Blocks of three minutes; swap roles, including the defender, after each block.
coaching_points: Take in everything before the ball arrives: colour, touches, defender.
If the defender blocks the gate, turn the other way and keep the ball.
After a mistake, say 'next', reset your body and be ready for the next ball.

media.caption: Check the coach's card while the ball travels, then turn through that colour

steps.label: P passes in; R checks over their shoulder to see the coach's card
The coach shows red: R receives across the body and turns left
Through the red gate on the left
R dribbles back and passes to P; the next one
Pass back to P, and swap roles after five

media.caption: Hardest: a defender, two cues at once, and 'next' after a mistake

steps.label: P passes in; R checks the card (a colour and a number of touches) and the defender's position
Blue and two: the defender is on the right, so R turns the other way, away from them
Second touch: R passes back to P
Mistake on the next one? Say 'next' and play again within three seconds

drills.title: Goalkeeper claims crosses from both wings
drills.summary: Crosses from both sides: the goalkeeper takes a good starting position, calls 'Keeper!' and catches the ball at its highest point.
drills.setup: A goal with a goalkeeper and two servers with balls, one on each wing about 14 m out. Servers throw crosses for younger goalkeepers, and kick them once they can deliver accurately.
instructions: The servers cross in turn, alternating sides.
The goalkeeper calls 'Keeper!' and claims the ball, catching it at the highest point.
The goalkeeper rolls it out to the other server and recovers to the goal.
Ten crosses each side, then rest or swap goalkeepers.
coaching_points: Start position: a step or two off the line, in the back half of the goal.
Watch the flight before you move, then call 'Keeper!' early and loud.
Attack the ball: take off from one foot, with the other knee up for protection.
Catch it in front of your head, at the highest point, and bring it into your chest.

variations.title: High throws from in front
variations.change: One server throws high underarm balls from 8 m in front, so the goalkeeper can practise the catch and the take-off.
variations.setup: A goal with a goalkeeper and one server with balls, 8 m out in front.
instructions: The server throws a high underarm ball to just in front of the goalkeeper.
The goalkeeper moves to it and catches it at the highest point.
Roll it back, return to the line and go again; ten throws.
coaching_points: Watch the ball all the way into your hands.
Jump off one foot with the other knee up.
Catch with the hands behind the ball in a W shape.

variations.title: Crosses from both wings
variations.change: Crosses from both wings: start position, call, claim.

variations.title: Claim or call 'Away!'
variations.change: A passive attacker and a defender in the box: the goalkeeper decides whether to claim or to stay and call 'Away!' for the defender.
variations.setup: As the base, plus a defender and a passive attacker in the six-yard area.
instructions: The servers cross in turn, mixing high and low crosses.
If the ball is within reach, the goalkeeper calls 'Keeper!' and claims it.
If not, the goalkeeper stays and calls 'Away!', and the defender clears it.
Outfield players play with their feet only in this drill: no headers. Heading has its own drill, for U12 and older, following the FA's heading guidance.
coaching_points: Decide early, and say it early: 'Keeper!' or 'Away!'.
Once you've called 'Keeper!', commit and go.
Low crosses you can't reach belong to the defender.

variations.title: 2v2 in the box
variations.change: Two attackers against two defenders in the box: the goalkeeper organises the defenders, claims when possible and punches when it's crowded.
variations.setup: As the base, plus two defenders and two attackers in the box.
instructions: The goalkeeper tells the defenders who to mark before each cross.
Attackers try to score from the cross; defenders and the goalkeeper stop them.
Claim the ball when you can; when it's crowded, punch it high and wide with both fists.
After a claim, look to start an attack with a quick throw to a server.
Outfield players play with their feet only in this drill: no headers. Heading has its own drill, for U12 and older, following the FA's heading guidance.
coaching_points: Organise before the cross: name the player and the job.
Claim if you can catch it cleanly; punch if bodies are in the way.
Punch through the bottom half of the ball, high and towards the side of the pitch.

media.caption: Easier: high throws from in front; catch at the highest point

steps.label: A high underarm throw to just in front of the goalkeeper
Roll it back and return to the line
A high throw to one side: move, then jump off one foot with the knee up

media.caption: Crosses from both wings: call 'Keeper!' and claim at the highest point

steps.label: The ball is on the right: a step off the line, in the back half of the goal
Cross from the right: call 'Keeper!', attack the ball and catch it at the highest point
Hold it, then roll it out to the left-hand server and recover to the goal
Cross from the left: claim again

media.caption: Harder: claim it, or stay and call 'Away!' for the defender

steps.label: A high cross from the right, between the attacker and the goal: 'Keeper!', and the goalkeeper claims it
Roll it out to the left-hand server; everyone resets
A low cross to the near post, out of the goalkeeper's reach: the goalkeeper stays and calls 'Away!'
The defender clears it with their foot

media.caption: Hardest: 2v2 in the box; the goalkeeper organises, then claims

steps.label: The ball is on the right; the goalkeeper tells the defenders who to mark
The attackers move to lose their markers as the server gets ready
A high cross into the middle: 'Keeper!', and the goalkeeper claims it above the players
Hold it, and look for a quick throw to start an attack

media.caption: Source: England Football – Goalkeeping: defending the area

drills.title: Goalkeeper 1v1 against a dribbler
drills.summary: An attacker dribbles at goal; the goalkeeper closes down, sets, stays big and smothers or saves.
drills.setup: A goal with a goalkeeper. An attacker 18 m out and a server behind them with the balls.
instructions: The server passes to the attacker, who dribbles at goal to score.
The goalkeeper closes down, sets as the attacker is about to touch the ball, and saves or smothers.
Attackers must not follow through into a goalkeeper who is on the ground.
Rotate attackers; six to eight goes for the goalkeeper, then rest or swap.
coaching_points: Close down while the ball is away from the attacker's foot; stop and set as they're about to touch it.
Set position: feet a little more than shoulder-width apart, weight forward, hands low.
Stay big and on your feet as long as you can: make the attacker decide.
Smother with your hands to the ball and your body behind it, head away from the boots; never dive head-first at feet.

variations.title: Attacker at jogging pace
variations.change: The attacker jogs the ball in from 12 m, and the goalkeeper practises closing down, setting and a safe smother, first from kneeling.
variations.setup: A goal with a goalkeeper. An attacker 12 m out with a ball, and a server with spare balls.
instructions: The attacker jogs the ball towards goal and doesn't speed up.
The goalkeeper closes down, sets, and smothers the ball when the attacker lets it run.
Practise the smother from kneeling first, then from standing.
Attackers don't shoot; six goes, then swap.
coaching_points: Close down while the ball is moving, set when the attacker is about to touch it.
Hands to the ball first, body behind it, head away from the boots.
Land on your side, not your front.

variations.title: Live 1v1 from 18 m
variations.change: A live 1v1: the attacker dribbles at goal from 18 m.

variations.title: From a narrow angle
variations.change: The attacker comes in from the side, so the goalkeeper has to cover the near post and narrow the angle.
variations.setup: A goal with a goalkeeper. The attacker starts wide, about 15 m out and 9 m to one side, with the server behind them.
instructions: The server passes to the attacker, who dribbles in from the side to score.
The goalkeeper moves into the line between ball and goal, closes down and sets.
Alternate sides every two goes.
Attackers must not follow through into a goalkeeper who is on the ground.
coaching_points: Get into the line between ball and goal before you close down.
Cover the near post: make them try to beat you at the far post.
Set before the shot; don't be moving when it's struck.

variations.title: A through ball: come out or stay
variations.change: The server plays a ball in behind a recovering defender; the goalkeeper decides whether to come out and get there first or stay and defend the 1v1.
variations.setup: A goal with a goalkeeper. An attacker and a defender about 16 m out, the server behind them with the balls.
instructions: The server plays a ball in behind the defender; the attacker and the defender race for it.
If the ball runs to the goalkeeper's side, the goalkeeper comes out and collects it first.
If the attacker gets there first, the goalkeeper defends the 1v1.
Attackers must not follow through into a goalkeeper who is on the ground.
coaching_points: Read the pass early: whose ball is it?
If you go, go fast and all the way; if you stay, get set.
Talk to the defender: 'Keeper's!' or 'Your ball!'.

media.caption: Close down while the ball is away from the attacker's foot, set, then smother

steps.label: The server passes to the attacker; the goalkeeper moves off the line as the ball travels
The attacker dribbles at goal; the goalkeeper keeps closing while the ball is away from their foot
The attacker is about to touch it: the goalkeeper sets, feet apart and hands low, staying big
A heavy touch: the goalkeeper spreads and smothers the ball, hands first

media.caption: Harder: from a narrow angle, cover the near post and stay big

steps.label: A pass to the attacker on the right; the goalkeeper moves into the line between ball and goal
The attacker dribbles in from the side; the goalkeeper closes down along that line
Set, with the near post covered
The shot goes at the near post: the goalkeeper, already set, saves and holds it

media.caption: Hardest: a through ball; come out and get there first, or stay

steps.label: The server plays a ball in behind the defender; attacker and defender race for it
The pass is overhit and runs towards goal: the goalkeeper comes off the line fast
The goalkeeper gets there first and gathers it before the attacker arrives

media.caption: Source: England Football – Goalkeeping: defending the space and the goal

drills.title: Races to the ball on the coach's call
drills.summary: Short races to a ball from different starting positions, then a finish: acceleration, deceleration and turning.
drills.setup: A 20 x 20 m area with a small goal at one end. Two players lie face down near the other end, side by side; the coach stands behind them with the balls. Do this early in the session, when players are fresh.
instructions: On 'Go!', both players jump up and sprint as the coach rolls a ball out in front of them.
First to the ball tries to score; the other defends.
Change the starting position each race: lying face down, sitting, kneeling, facing away.
Each race is about five seconds; walk back and rest for 30–40 seconds before the next. Six to eight races each.
coaching_points: Push off hard with short, powerful first steps; drive the arms.
Stay low as you get up; lean forward to accelerate.
To stop or turn, take short, quick steps and lower your hips.
Growing fast and something hurts? Stop and tell the coach: don't play through pain.

variations.title: Start, stop and turn on calls
variations.change: No ball: players sprint, stop and turn on the coach's calls, learning to accelerate and slow down well.
variations.setup: A start line and a line of cones 8 m away. Players spread out along the start line.
instructions: 'Go!': sprint forward.
'Stop!': stop as quickly as you can, low and balanced.
'Turn!': turn and sprint back to the start line.
Mix the calls up; rest for 30 seconds between goes.
coaching_points: Lean forward and drive the arms to start.
Stop with short, quick steps and bend the knees.
Turn on the balls of your feet, not your heels.

variations.title: Race to the ball from different starts
variations.change: Up from lying, sitting or kneeling, race to a rolled ball and score.

variations.title: Mirror, then sprint
variations.change: No ball: the attacker tries to lose a defender who mirrors them between two cones, then sprints for one of two gates.
variations.setup: Two cones 6 m apart. The attacker and the defender face each other, 4 m apart, between the cones; two gates 8 m behind the defender.
instructions: The attacker shuffles side to side between the cones; the defender mirrors them.
When the attacker has lost the defender, they sprint for either gate.
The defender tries to touch them before they get there.
Swap roles after each go; rest for 30–40 seconds between goes.
coaching_points: Attacker: change speed as well as direction to lose the defender.
Defender: stay low on the balls of your feet, and watch the hips, not the feet.
Push off the outside foot to change direction.

variations.title: Race, then 1v1 to two goals
variations.change: The coach rolls the ball in from the side; the winner of the race attacks one goal, and if the other wins it back, they attack the other goal.
variations.setup: A 20 x 24 m area with a small goal at each end. Two players sit on one side facing away; the coach stands on the other side with the balls.
instructions: On 'Go!', both players get up and race for the ball the coach rolls in.
The first to it attacks the far goal; if the other wins the ball back, they attack the near goal.
The race ends with a goal or after ten seconds.
Each race is about five seconds; walk back and rest for 30–40 seconds before the next. Six to eight races each.
coaching_points: Get up and turn in one movement.
If you lose the race, recover goal-side as quickly as you can.
Accelerate away after winning the ball.

media.caption: Easier: start, stop and turn on the coach's calls, no ball

steps.label: 'Go!': sprint forward
'Stop!': short, quick steps, low and balanced
'Turn!': turn and sprint back to the start line

media.caption: Up from lying down, race to the ball and score

steps.label: Both lie face down; on 'Go!' they jump up and sprint as the coach rolls the ball out
First to the ball shields it and drives at the goal
Score in the small goal
Walk back for full rest before the next race

media.caption: Harder: lose the mirroring defender, then sprint through a gate

steps.label: The attacker shuffles right; the defender mirrors
A quick change of direction to the left; the defender follows
Back right and away: sprint for the right-hand gate

media.caption: Hardest: race to the ball, then play 1v1 to two goals

steps.label: Sitting down facing away; on 'Go!' both get up as the coach rolls the ball in
P1 gets there first and attacks the far goal; P2 recovers goal-side
P2 wins the ball and attacks the other goal
P2 turns and drives at the near goal
P2 scores

drills.title: 3v3 games in four-minute blocks
drills.summary: Short 3v3 games with four small goals and the ball always in play, in four-minute blocks with rest between them.
drills.setup: A 20 x 25 m pitch with two small goals at each end. Two teams of three; the coach stands on the side with lots of balls.
instructions: Play 3v3; each team attacks the two goals at the far end.
When the ball goes out or a goal is scored, the coach plays a new ball straight in, so play hardly stops.
Four games of four minutes, with three minutes' rest between them: walk, drink, keep-ups.
Two pitches side by side for twelve players.
coaching_points: Keep moving to support the player on the ball.
Lose the ball? Press straight away.
Get back into position quickly after an attack.
For younger players, the game itself is enough: never use running as a punishment.

variations.title: 4v4, three-minute games
variations.change: 4v4 with three games of three minutes and substitutes rotating on, so each player works less and rests more.
variations.setup: A 20 x 25 m pitch with two small goals at each end. Two teams of four, with any extra players as substitutes; the coach stands on the side with lots of balls.
instructions: Play 4v4; each team attacks the two goals at the far end.
The coach plays a new ball straight in when the ball goes out or a goal is scored.
Three games of three minutes, with three minutes' rest; substitutes rotate on every minute.
Two pitches side by side for more players.

variations.title: 3v3, four four-minute games
variations.change: 3v3, four games of four minutes, three minutes' rest.

variations.title: Less rest
variations.change: The same games, with two minutes' rest between them instead of three.
instructions: Play 3v3; each team attacks the two goals at the far end.
The coach plays a new ball straight in when the ball goes out or a goal is scored.
Four games of four minutes, with two minutes' rest between them.
Two pitches side by side for twelve players.

variations.title: Whole team in the attacking half
variations.change: A goal only counts if the whole team is in the attacking half, so every player has to keep making forward and recovery runs.
variations.setup: A 20 x 25 m pitch with two small goals at each end and halfway marked with cones. Two teams of three; the coach stands on the side with lots of balls.
instructions: Play 3v3; each team attacks the two goals at the far end.
A goal only counts if all three attackers are in the attacking half.
Four games of four minutes, with two minutes' rest between them.
The coach plays a new ball straight in after every goal or ball out.
coaching_points: Push up as a team when you attack.
Sprint back as soon as you lose the ball: you're the furthest from your own goals.
Keep working for the whole four minutes: the last minute counts most.

media.caption: Easier: 4v4, three games of three minutes, with substitutes rotating on

steps.label: The coach plays a ball in to A4; the others move to give options
A4 passes inside to A3, who has space; team B shuffles across
A3 sets it to A1, arriving in support
A1 scores in one of team B's goals

media.caption: 3v3 with four small goals: lose the ball, press straight away

steps.label: The coach plays a ball straight in to team A
A2 passes inside to A3; the others move to support
B3 intercepts: team B attacks straight away and team A presses
B3 passes wide to B2, who is free; team A sprint back
B2 scores in one of team A's goals

media.caption: Hardest: a goal only counts with the whole team in the attacking half

steps.label: Team A builds from their own half
A1 drives forward; A2 and A3 push up over halfway
A1 passes to A2; A3 keeps running so the whole team is in the half
A2 scores: it counts, because all three are in the attacking half
